description.value: Ripple Ridge Cabin is a backcountry wilderness hut in the Kootenays, situated within the Ripple Ridge Recreation Site and managed by the volunteer Ripple Ridge Recreation Association in partnership with Recreation Sites and Trails BC. It sits about 3.2 km from the Kootenay Pass parking area and is one of two cabins (the other being Lightning Strike Cabin) located just 50 metres apart at high elevation. Reservation is required and summer access via the Maryland FSR is subject to snow until early July, making this a destination suited to self-sufficient adventure cyclists rather than casual touring.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The website confirms this is a reservation-only wilderness cabin managed by the Ripple Ridge Recreation Association under agreement with Recreation Sites and Trails BC, with email contact rippleridgehut@gmail.com and an active booking system. The amenities page is referenced via a link but its content was not captured in the fetch, so specific amenity details (bike storage, laundry, charging, etc.) cannot be confirmed. Access details on the /map subpage show the cabin is reached by a 3.2km non-motorized trail in winter or via a rough 27km forest service road in summer, making this a backcountry hut with no on-site staff implied.
concerns: Cabin amenities subpage was not captured in the website fetch — bike storage and other amenity details remain unverifiable.
No on-site staff implied; volunteer-managed hut with email-only contact (rippleridgehut@gmail.com).
Winter access route passes through Stagleap Provincial Park, which is explicitly designated as a non-motorized area — cycling access rules unclear.
Summer FSR access (Maryland FSR, ~27 km) is rough and unsuitable for low-clearance vehicles; suitability for loaded touring bikes is uncertain.
No phone number or physical address available in OSM or on website.
High elevation means seasonal access limitations (road typically clear early July to early October).
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: This is a remote backcountry wilderness hut with no on-site staff, challenging access (3.2km non-motorized trail or 27km rough FSR), and no verified bike-specific amenities — the cabin amenities page was referenced but its content was not captured in the fetch. It may suit self-sufficient bikepacking cyclists but is unlikely to meet WWC required criteria without further investigation.
enrichment_extras.notes: The site also manages a second cabin (Lightning Strike Cabin) at the same recreation site. Enricher should verify whether a separate OSM record exists for Lightning Strike Cabin to avoid duplicate listings.
